context: I Question. Let X = (X1 , X2 , . . . , Xk ) be an ε-biased distribution over (Fn2 )k . Let U be uniform over Fn2 . Let f1 , f2 , . . . , fk be functions from {0, 1}n → {0, 1} with expectations µ1 , µ2 , . . . , µk . Is it true that Y Y | E [ fi (U + Xi )] − µi | ≤ ε0 U,X i≤k i≤k for an ε0 which is independent of n and that, say, goes to 0 for any fixed k and vanishing ε? Note that the Xi may be correlated. It can be shown that the distribution D + E in Theorem 1.1, when D is linear, has the above format, by writing the generator matrix in systematic form. (In fact, it is the sum of several independent samples of such distributions.)
